decisions.thought: Choice Scarf Gholdengo applies huge immediate pressure with Shadow Ball and Make It Rain. Garchomp and Primarina provide strong coverage against Kingambit, Incineroar, and their Dragons.

Incineroar lead is safest with Intimidate plus Fake Out to break Mimikyu disguise and Taunt to stop Volcarona setup. Dragonite covers opposing Dragonite and Garchomp with Ice Punch and Gholdengo with Earthquake. Primarina covers Volcarona, Garchomp, and opposing Primarina.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Evaluating Gen 9 singles team matchup and lead options for a bring-6 pick-3 format.Assessing Incineroar lead viability and finalizing the three-Pokémon core with coverage tradeoffs.

decisions.thought: Incineroar threatens Gholdengo with its dual STABs, and Focus Blast is inaccurate and unlikely to OHKO specially defensive Incineroar. Primarina resists both of Incineroar's STAB types and takes minimal damage on switch-in.

Good as Gold blocks Taunt and Parting Shot, and Fake Out can't hit Ghost. Incineroar resists both STABs so this is a good matchup to stay in. Flare Blitz is super effective and the only move that works.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Evaluating Incineroar versus Gholdengo matchup and move interactions under ability and type constraints.Comparing Flare Blitz damage against Gholdengo with switching to Dragonite or Primarina.

decisions.thought: Primarina has a massive type advantage against Incineroar. Liquid Voice Hyper Voice is STAB and super effective, dealing massive damage or knocking it out if it stays in.
Incineroar is in a bad matchup to stay in, weak to both Water and Fairy STAB from Primarina. Parting Shot lets me pivot out while dropping its offenses for my switch-in.

decisions.thought: Dragonite takes super-effective Fairy damage and would lose Multiscale, a bad matchup to switch into. Our Primarina resists Water and takes neutral Fairy, walling their Primarina while preserving Dragonite.

decisions.thought: Primarina is at -1 SpA from Parting Shot, losing the mirror trade. Switching to Gholdengo is safe against Fairy moves, and it threatens heavy damage next turn.
Opponent Primarina is at -1 SpA and its Water STAB is resisted by my Primarina, so this is a free setup turn. Switching to Incineroar or Dragonite risks a bad matchup into Water or Fairy coverage.

decisions.thought: Primarina is already at +1 SpD, so Make It Rain will not OHKO and will sharply reduce Gholdengo's Special Attack while locking it in. Tricking Choice Scarf completely cripples the setup Primarina and strips its ability to freely boost or switch moves.

Gholdengo threatens a super-effective Steel hit on Primarina and resists Moonblast. Incineroar resists both Steel and Ghost and hits back super-effectively. This is a bad matchup to stay in, so hard switch.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Comparing damage and type matchups to choose between Sparkling Aria, Moonblast, Calm Mind, and Flip Turn for Primarina versus Gholdengo.Evaluating Gholdengo's speed and resistances against Primarina's move options.Comparing a hard switch to Incineroar against Flip Turn for pivoting while weighing damage risk.

decisions.thought: Incineroar now holds Choice Scarf and likely outspeeds Gholdengo, threatening an immediate knockout with Flare Blitz or Knock Off. Primarina easily resists both of Incineroar's STAB attacks.

Incineroar resists both Steel and Ghost STAB, so this is a bad matchup to switch out of. Good as Gold blocks Parting Shot and Taunt and Fake Out is immune, leaving Flare Blitz as the only working option. With Scarf speed it should hit first for a super-effective likely knockout.

decisions.thought: Incineroar is locked into Flare Blitz due to Choice Scarf. Primarina easily survives another resisted hit and threatens an easy knockout with Liquid Voice Hyper Voice.

Incineroar is locked into resisted Flare Blitz and weak to Water Hyper Voice, a bad matchup. Speed is uncertain with Scarf vs Primarina range, risking a KO before moving. Dragonite resists Water and has full HP Multiscale to safely absorb.

decisions.thought: Dragonite is faster than Primarina, so speed is the deciding factor. Earthquake threatens a knockout before a likely Moonblast. Mega evolving boosts damage to secure it.

decisions.thought: Dragonite is faster than Primarina and will KO it, but Dragonite is at 1% HP. Priority Aqua Jet easily finishes it off before it can move.

Dragonite at 1 HP dies to any attack and ExtremeSpeed cannot KO Primarina from 39%. This is a bad matchup to stay in. Switching to our Primarina resists their STABs and preserves ExtremeSpeed for later.

decisions.thought: Opposing Primarina is neutral to Fairy and weak to Sp. Atk drops. Moonblast does solid neutral STAB damage while conserving our full-health backline of Gholdengo and Mega Garchomp.
Opposing Primarina is at 44% and Moonblast is neutral while Sparkling Aria is resisted, so Moonblast gives the likely knockout. Switching to Incineroar risks a super-effective Water move.

decisions.thought: Gholdengo is faster than Primarina and easily finishes it off with Make It Rain while resisting Moonblast.
Gholdengo is faster than Primarina and Make It Rain easily secures the knockout from 41% HP.
Gholdengo outspeeds and resists Moonblast, so this is a bad matchup to stay in. Primarina is low and valuable later, while Incineroar resists Steel and Ghost.

decisions.thought: Incineroar holds Choice Scarf and threatens Gholdengo with super-effective STAB. Switching directly to full-health Garchomp handles Incineroar's Fire moves easily and sets up an endgame sweep against their remaining weakened team.
Flare Blitz is super effective and should knock out Gholdengo. Taunt and Parting Shot are blocked by Good as Gold, and Fake Out is immune vs Ghost.

decisions.thought: Incineroar is locked into Flare Blitz, at 28% HP, and will faint either from Earthquake or recoil/Rough Skin. Not Mega Evolving preserves Garchomp's higher base speed against the remaining bench.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
**Analyzing Speed Stats**

I'm currently focused on speed comparisons, specifically between Garchomp and Incineroar. My initial assumption about Garchomp outspeeding Choice Scarf Incineroar was off – it needs to be Jolly to reach an effective speed of 184. Mega Garchomp is notably slower, dropping to base 92. Need to verify that Incineroar even has Choice Scarf.

decisions.thought: Incineroar is locked into not-very-effective Flare Blitz and will die to attack plus Rough Skin plus recoil anyway. Switching 41% Primarina into Garchomp risks a likely knockout from Earthquake, so sacrifice Incineroar for chip and a free switch.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Evaluating the Pokémon battle rules and selecting a single legal action based on speed, knockout, or matchup.Applying the choice-lock constraint to rule out illegal moves and keep only the valid switch.Evaluating speed tie risk with Choice Scarf and the safer sacrifice-then-switch sequence.

decisions.thought: Dragonite is Flying-type and immune to Garchomp's revealed Earthquake, while Primarina is slower and would be knocked out before moving. Sacrificing the 1 HP Dragonite to block Ground preserves Primarina for later.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Analyzing the battle state to select a legal switch between Primarina and Dragonite-Mega given HP and moves.Evaluating damage ranges and speed to confirm Primarina is the only viable switch despite likely being KOed.Assessing whether sacking low-HP Dragonite preserves Primarina versus immediate KO risk from Garchomp.Comparing sacking 1HP Dragonite versus sending Primarina to induce a potential Garchomp switch.Evaluating Dragonite's Ground immunity to safely absorb Earthquake and enable a favorable follow-up.

decisions.thought: Dragonite-Mega is at 1% HP, and base Garchomp outspeeds it naturally (169 Spe vs max 167 Spe). Mega Evolution would lower Garchomp's Speed to 158, risking being outsped, and Outrage locks Garchomp into the opposing Primarina. Stone Edge secures the knockout without locking into Outrage.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
**Analyzing Battle Scenario**

I've been calculating the battle scenario. Currently, Dragonite-Mega has 1% HP, and base Garchomp is confirmed to outspeed. Evolving Garchomp, however, risks Dragonite moving first, which I must factor. Stone Edge's 80% accuracy adds another layer of probability.

decisions.thought: Dragonite is at 1 HP and speed versus Garchomp is uncertain, so it could be KO'd before moving. ExtremeSpeed's +2 priority guarantees damage before dying.

decisions.thought: Dragonite fainted so a forced switch to the last Pokemon is required. There is no speed decision with only Primarina left to face Garchomp.

Garchomp is faster and will likely knockout with Earthquake before Primarina moves. Moonblast is super effective and gives the only chance to knockout back if it picks Stone Edge or misses.
